claims.claim: Reasoning LLMs did not have better in-advance confidence estimates than non-reasoning LLMs on single-step coding and multi-step tasks.
claims.stance_target: R1 candidate L2; component verdict: NARROW (verbal only)
claims.quoted_support: reasoning LLMs perform comparably to or worse than non-reasoning LLMs.

claims.claim: With in-context experience of failure some but not all LLMs reduce overconfidence, improving decisions; decisions are approximately rational given stated probabilities.
claims.stance_target: R1 candidate L3; component verdict: NARROW
claims.quoted_support: With in-context experiences of failure, some but not all LLMs reduce their overconfidence leading to significantly improved decision making, while others do not.

claims.claim: On SWE-bench Verified, after each tool call the LLM restates success probability; Claude models degrade in discrimination and grow more overconfident while most OpenAI models modestly improve.
claims.stance_target: R1 candidate L3; component verdict: NARROW
claims.quoted_support: most OpenAI models show modest improvements in their discriminatory power as they progress through the tasks, while Claude models show degradation in discriminatory power and increasing overconfidence
